analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: MELT 20 Nov 2026
key_insights: US equities sold off into the weekend. SPX retested the 7,000 level with pressure led by AI and semiconductors. Late-day headlines on an NVDA SEC probe, hawkish Washington officials, and an FT report that Israel is urging Trump to restart strikes on Iran added to the move.
The tape was already fragile after capital markets activity did not provide the stabilizing support for risk appetite that many had expected.

Trading activity was not proportional to the size of the price moves. The desk points to elevated top-down macro trading (ETFs above 39% of tape volume) and thin top-of-book liquidity (S&P at $4mm, near the YTD low).
The desk saw steady long-only sell tickets in semiconductors with buyers absent. Panic is still anecdotal but intensifying, and the Nasdaq VIX is at its highest level since COVID.
Hedge funds and long-only accounts were moderate net sellers on the week. The main debate is what catalyst could put a bottom in price action.

S&P 500 closed lower for a 7th consecutive session, a streak not seen since Feb 2020 and one of only 5 instances in the last 25 years. The index is down about 8.6% on the week, the first such week since Apr 4 (early in the Iran War) and the second worst week since COVID.

CTAs are estimated at net short -$19bn of US equity length (S&P at the 26th percentile rank) after selling $57bn over the past month. Forecasts show CTAs selling in every scenario over the next week, with SPX trigger levels of 7596 / 7540 / 7119 (short/medium/long-term).

Next week the S&P implied move through Friday 11/27 is 3.27%. Tuesday night tech earnings in focus are DELL, WDAY, HPQ, with consumer earnings continuing (BBY, DKS, BURL, DLTR, ANF, URBN on Tuesday). US markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close at 1pm on Friday.

Prime book data for Nov 13-19: hedge funds net sold US equities for a 3rd straight week (6 of the last 7), driven by heavy shorting in single stocks and, to a lesser extent, ETFs, partly offset by long buying in index products.

ETF short flows rose 11% this week after a 8.6% decline in the prior week, the largest percentage shorting since March. Single stocks were shorted every day this week, the largest weekly shorting since Jun 2022 and the third largest in the past decade.
9 of 11 sectors were net sold in prime data, excluding Info Tech and Energy. Financials, Consumer Discretionary, Real Estate and Communication Services led the selling.
